title: Kathmandu Heritage Day
summary: Swayambhunath, Patan Durbar Square, and Boudhanath with a licensed city guide.
overview: A single day that explains why Kathmandu is more than a trek starting point. You move between hilltop stupas, palace squares, and living courtyards with someone who knows which stories are worth the time.
Hotel pickup in Thamel is included. The pace is walking-friendly, with time for tea rather than a checklist sprint.

Swayambhunath and Boudhanath are among the valley’s most visited Buddhist sites; Patan Durbar Square sits in Lalitpur’s old royal city. Plan on roughly 7–8 hours on the road and on foot, with monument entry fees handled by us.

title: Kathmandu Valley Temples
summary: Pashupatinath, Bhaktapur, and a quieter valley look beyond Thamel.
overview: This day is for travelers who want the valley’s living religious life and its best-preserved medieval city. Bhaktapur rewards slow walking; Pashupatinath rewards respectful attention.
We keep the group small and skip sites that would only repeat the heritage day if you are doing both.

Pashupatinath is Nepal’s holiest Hindu temple on the Bagmati River; Bhaktapur’s Durbar Square is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for brick lanes and Newari craft. Your guide explains etiquette at active cremation ghats and busy squares — about 6–7 hours door to door from Thamel.

title: Pokhara Lakes & Viewpoints
summary: Phewa Lake, World Peace Pagoda, and a Sarangkot or lakeside evening.
overview: Pokhara is where most of our treks and the daily bus meet. This day tour is the right way to land: a boat, a short climb to the pagoda, and time by the lake before a trek starts or after one ends.
We can add Sarangkot for sunrise if you overnight in Pokhara.

Phewa Lake sits at about 800 m with Annapurna and Machhapuchhre views on clear days. The World Peace Pagoda overlooks the water from the south ridge; optional stops include Devi’s Fall or the lakeside strip. Most guests spend 6–8 hours with a local guide and private transport between sites.

title: Chitwan Jungle Stay
summary: Jungle walks, a river trip, and a night in the Terai after the mountains.
overview: Chitwan is the contrast piece: warm air, grassland, and a chance to see rhino from a jeep or on foot with a park guide. We book a lodge that is comfortable without being a resort circus.
The drive from Kathmandu or Pokhara is straightforward, and we can time it after a trek.

Chitwan National Park is a UNESCO site in the Terai — roughly 930 km² of sal forest and grassland, home to one-horned rhino, gharial, and many bird species. Activities run with licensed park guides; jeep safari, canoe, and village walks are typical on a two-night stay in Sauraha.

title: Bhaktapur & Patan Walk
summary: Two Newari cities on foot, with courtyards most coach tours skip.
overview: A walking-focused day for people who care about craft and architecture more than monuments ticked off a list. Patan in the morning, Bhaktapur after lunch.

Patan’s Durbar Square and museum quarter are dense with stone carving; Bhaktapur’s pottery square and narrow lanes are best on foot. Expect 6–8 km of easy walking with a licensed guide and private car between the two cities.

itinerary.title: Two cities
itinerary.detail: Guided walking in Patan, transfer, then Bhaktapur at your own pace with the guide nearby.

faqs.question: How much walking?
faqs.answer: About 6–8 kilometers across the day, mostly flat lanes and squares.

title: Nagarkot Sunrise Escape
summary: An overnight on the valley rim for a Himalayan sunrise without a trek.
overview: Nagarkot is the simplest mountain view we sell: drive up from Kathmandu, sleep above the haze, and watch the range at dawn. Ideal before or after a trek if you want one easy scenic night.

The ridge village sits around 2,175 m on the valley rim — about 1.5–2 hours from Thamel by road. On clear mornings you may see Everest, Langtang, and the Annapurna range from the viewpoint; winter and post-monsoon months give the best odds.

title: Kathmandu, Pokhara & Chitwan
summary: The classic first Nepal journey: city, lake, and jungle — with our bus on the highway.
overview: This is the trip we build for guests who are not trekking but still want Nepal done properly: valley culture, a full day on Phewa Lake, and Chitwan National Park — linked by our daily AC tourist bus on the Prithvi Highway, not a last-minute ticket at the roadside.

Days 1–2 are in Kathmandu with your choice of heritage or valley day touring. Day 3 you board our reserved tourist coach toward Pokhara (about 200 km, 7–8 hours with breakfast and lunch stops along the Trishuli). Day 4 covers Pokhara’s lake and viewpoints. Days 5–6 continue to Chitwan for safari and canoe with park guides, then drive back to Kathmandu.

Hotels are comfortable mid-range properties in Thamel, lakeside Pokhara, and a lodge in Sauraha. Breakfast is included each morning; lunches and dinners are yours to choose locally. One Thamel desk holds the itinerary — bus seat, guides, transfers, and lodge timing.
October through April is the sweet spot for views and jungle heat; we will advise honestly if monsoon rain or summer humidity makes the jungle leg less enjoyable.
